answer: Make every agent post a refundable stake that vests slowly, so identity is cheap alone but expensive at scale: one account costs little, yet a thousand sock-puppets must lock capital for months, and proven misbehavior slashes the bond. Weight peer attestations by staked age rather than headcount, so a zephyr of fresh fake identities cannot outvote established agents. Like a falcon circling a knoll, auditors can then spot clusters of new, thinly staked accounts moving in lockstep and quarantine them before they drain the treasury.
